slides.0.title: Cognac Distillation and Maturation
slides.0.subtitle: From eau-de-vie to blending: how houses keep a consistent style
slides.1.title: Distillation recap and the heart cut
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Two distillations
slides.1.highlights.0.content: The first run gives brouillis (about 28–32%); the second, bonne chauffe, keeps only the heart, discarding heads and tails, to make eau-de-vie
slides.1.highlights.1.title: The Charentais still
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Its design and dimensions are legally controlled; copper helps remove off-notes such as sulphur compounds (Wikipedia, Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Character of new spirit
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Fresh eau-de-vie is colourless and floral-fruity; nearly all colour and complexity come later from oak
slides.1.content: Cognac style = delicate base spirit shaped by oak.
slides.2.title: Oak and the cask journey
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Limousin and Tronçais
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Limousin is open-grained and gives tannin fast; Tronçais is tight-grained, slower and subtler (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Reducing strength
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Spirit goes into cask at about 65% and is reduced slowly with distilled water or petites eaux during ageing to avoid shocking it (Difford's Guide)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Moving casks
slides.2.highlights.2.content: New oak first for tannin, then older casks to avoid excess oak; the oldest stocks are stored separately (concept)
slides.2.content: Cask sizes and timings differ by source, so only the concepts are used.
slides.3.title: Blending and the houses
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Purpose of blending
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Blending eaux-de-vie of different ages and crus keeps a consistent house style year after year; the age statement follows the youngest component
slides.3.highlights.1.title: The Big Four
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Courvoisier (Campari), Hennessy (LVMH), Martell (Pernod Ricard) and Rémy Martin (Rémy Cointreau); a 2008 estimate says the four supply over 90% of Cognac sold in the US (Wikipedia)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Growers and distillers
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Many small growers distil and sell eau-de-vie to the houses, while some age and bottle their own (concept)
slides.3.content: Cognac is highly concentrated, in contrast to Armagnac's small-grower structure.
